opened.title: feat(launcher): scaffold a desktop launcher for all four games
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
A Tauri 2 desktop app in `launcher/` that puts OpenRAC behind buttons for every version in `games/` (rac1 PAL and NTSC-U, rac2, rac3, rac4): find your discs, place each build's inputs, set up, build, check, play in PCSX2, and open the level editor. It runs the checkout's own tools and streams their output; it hard-codes nothing a `game.json` already says.

This is **scaffolding**: the app, its look, the catalogue, the job runner and the repository-wide actions work; most per-game actions are written from each game's docs but not yet run from the launcher. `launcher/docs/INTEGRATION.md` is the handoff for connecting them.

## What's in it

- **`launcher/core/`** (Rust, no window): the catalogue from `games/*/game.json` and `progress/summary.json`; each version's disc and input status (names, sizes, links; never hashes an image); settings; detection of the checkout, Python, PCSX2, Godot and Docker; a job runner that streams output and cancels a job's whole process tree.

merged.title: Stop helping the compiler, plus another 1.9% of the game
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
## The part everyone will read

Turns out a few of our build steps were doing GCC 2.95's homework for it. Apparently a 25-year-old compiler is supposed to suffer alone, so now it does.

What's gone:
- `fix_tail_calls.py`, `fix_trunc_slot.py` and `fix_core_spills.py`, which touched up the compiler's output after the fact.
- Per-function flags. GCC 2.95 only takes flags per file, so now we do too (`config/file_cflags.txt`). Four level functions moved into files of their own to keep theirs. Level files are our own grouping anyway; retail never saw them.

We measured the damage before deleting anything. 12 functions depended on all of it: 2,404 bytes, 0.06% of the code. Seven still match with a whole-file flag. Five (620 bytes) are assembly again, including `_exit`, all 8 bytes of it, so `core/crt0` is no longer a complete unit. Our condolences to crt0.

The `ps2eeas` emulation stays, and now it comes with receipts. We never used SN's real assembler because it died with a stack o

merged.title: Twenty Haikus walk into a decomp: 41 more functions, plus GPT's movie work
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
## What happened

We pointed up to twenty Haiku agents at every level function nobody had matched yet, smallest first, and let them run until the queue was empty. They are cheap and fast, and they are about as good at long functions as you'd expect.

How it went, by size:
- Up to about 1 KB, small functions retried and untried ones: 21 exact.
- 1.5 to 1.8 KB: 3 exact.
- 1.7 to 4 KB: 0 of 128. They get within a few bytes and then argue with the register allocator until their budget runs out.

So the cheap tier works on small functions and stops at around 1.5 KB. Its closest attempts are staged in `nonmatching/` for whoever wants to finish them. Several are 4 to 12 bytes off or a single register swap away.

Patterns they found that worked, all plain C:
- An unused local array reproduces a gap retail leaves in its stack frame (func_L04_002CF440 is the shortest example: one call and a `char buf[80]`).
- Writing switch cases in retail's block order, with a label for every state, keeps the j

- The eight staged `nonmatching/` files for these functions are removed and the README is regenerated.

Plain C only, no inline asm, pins or barriers, no Sony SDK material, and `src/game/movie/` is untouched. Matched wit

merged.title: campaign: retain bounded C4130 new-function refusals
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Record a bounded C4130/Qwen experiment on two genuinely uncovered boot functions, with all refusals retained and no source integration or C coverage change.

- `FUN_001302E0`: three semantically valid proposals reproduce the same 32-byte body with six differing bytes; the loop stops on the repeated compiled result.
- `FUN_00131760`: one semantically valid proposal produces 28 bytes against the complete 32-byte reference; unsupported and repeated proposals remain in the private research trace.
- Selection checked Ghidra function boundaries, caller dataflow, all 28 published proof files and existing register history. Target-specific native probes exercise signed-shift edge cases and all 256 byte values without assuming valid BCD digits.

Only the canonical experiment register and its generated queue change. Candidate sources, retail bytes, tools and compiler artifacts remain private. Full-image integration was not attempted and no matching credit is added.

Validation: 110 campaign tests

This records ownership and planning only. It adds zero matching or integration credit, changes no C source or compiler profile, and does not merge the Qwen research branch. The queue is regenerated through the maintained campaign tool.

Validation: 110 campaign tests pass; generated campaign views and proof-derived README progress checks pass; scoped diff/privacy checks pass. Original game data, selection receipts and runtime paths remain private.

merged.title: docs: explain updating contributor branches before review
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## What this changes

The beginner guide now explicitly explains how to update an existing contribution
branch when upstream `RAC2` advances. Contributors preserve local work, verify
their upstream remote, fetch and merge the current target, then regenerate and
validate affected source/proof/progress outputs before requesting review.

The instructions address the generated-file reconciliation needed during #54.
They retain both contributors' changes and experiment history, link the maintained
workflows, require a normal fork push and CI on the final commit, and keep private
bindings local. Documentation-only changes use documentation checks.

- [ ] Tooling or workflow changes

  the following section number.
